split_decision.statement: chap05 fits B4 as a whole file (319-337 prose lines against a 360 ceiling) but does NOT fit B5. Authoring the whole chapter at the atomicity this series uses yields 46 accepted candidates against a B5 ceiling of 40.
split_decision.policy_applied: book-batch-05-sources.json selection_budget.B5.escalation_trigger: 'If authoring exceeds 40 accepted candidates, do NOT raise B5 again. Split the source and re-inventory.' B5 is therefore left at 40 and the source is split.
split_decision.split_point: L427, the ## 컨슈머 그룹 관리 scope boundary. It is a top-level heading and the chapter's natural seam: everything before it concerns the AdminClient object itself, its configuration and topic administration; everything after concerns consumer groups, cluster metadata, advanced operations and testing.
split_decision.resulting_sizes: batch 06 = 25 candidates over L7-426; batch 07 = a projected 21 candidates over L427-870.
split_decision.why_not_consolidate: Merging candidates to land under 40 in one batch would fuse distinct API operations (describeConfigs vs incrementalAlterConfigs, the two client.dns.lookup modes) into composite notes, contradicting the project rule that one atomic concept is one file.

namespace_decision.rationale: chap05 introduces the AdminClient API surface, which no applied concept covers. 22 of 25 candidates are operations or properties of that API and take the new namespace.
namespace_decision.reused_namespace: kafka.config.* takes the three client-side configuration parameters (client.dns.lookup and its two modes, request.timeout.ms). The applied kafka.config.* set is broker-side, but the namespace is keyed on 'this is a named configuration parameter', not on which side sets it.
namespace_decision.path_convention: kafka.adminclient.adminclient maps to kafka/adminclient/kafka-adminclient.md, following the applied kafka.zookeeper.zookeeper -> kafka/zookeeper/kafka-zookeeper.md and kafka.retention.retention -> kafka/retention/message-retention.md precedent that keeps a note's basename distinct from its folder name.

id_rules.concept_id: lowercase dot-separated domain.subdomain.concept; the concept segment is the API method, configuration key or property name as it appears in the source
id_rules.canonical_path: content/brain/knowledge/<domain>/<subdomain>/<slug>.md with an ASCII slug, so the URL stays ASCII while the displayed title stays Korean
id_rules.tags: derived, never authored: the engine requires tags to equal the canonical path's folder segments below content/brain/knowledge/

review_flag_policy.conflict: The candidate's evidence lies in the same domain as an applied concept that batch 06 touches, so U3 must confirm it relates rather than restates.
review_flag_policy.low-confidence: The cited span carries three or fewer prose lines, or the concept boundary is an authoring judgement over a container anchor.
review_flag_policy.provenance-warning: The evidence span is not plain prose: it opens on a fenced code block, an Obsidian callout, or the pre-heading preamble that has no heading_chain.
review_flag_policy.sampling_note: Every flagged candidate must be fully sampled at U3.

candidates.title: AdminClient
candidates.concept_granularity: single programmatic administration API for Kafka that returns Result objects and takes Options objects, replacing the pre-AdminClient workarounds for managing topics and cluster state

candidates.title: AdminClient 비동기 작동
candidates.concept_granularity: single asynchronous execution model in which every AdminClient method returns one or more Future objects wrapped in a Result object

candidates.title: 최종적 일관성
candidates.concept_granularity: single consistency guarantee under which an AdminClient Future completes when the controller's state is updated, leaving the moment every broker learns of the change unspecified

candidates.title: Options 객체
candidates.concept_granularity: single per-method parameter object carrying how the broker should handle that AdminClient request

candidates.title: timeoutMs
candidates.concept_granularity: single per-request timeout parameter every AdminClient method inherits because all Options classes extend AbstractOptions

candidates.title: 카프카 어드민 프로토콜
candidates.concept_granularity: single implementation contract in which KafkaAdminClient builds Kafka admin protocol messages directly, so an operation absent from the interface is genuinely unimplemented

candidates.title: AdminClient 수평구조
candidates.concept_granularity: single structural property of the admin surface in which resources are plain string or numeric identifiers with no object dependency, hierarchy or namespace

candidates.title: 어드민 작업 라우팅
candidates.concept_granularity: single routing rule sending state-changing admin operations to the controller and read-only ones to whichever broker is least loaded from the client's view

candidates.title: AdminClient 생명주기
candidates.concept_granularity: single create-configure-close lifecycle whose only mandatory property is the cluster bootstrap URI and whose untimed close waits for every in-flight operation

candidates.title: client.dns.lookup
candidates.concept_granularity: single client-side setting governing how bootstrap hostnames are resolved, needed because clients reconnect using the hostnames advertised.listeners returns

candidates.title: resolve_canonical_bootstrap_servers_only
candidates.concept_granularity: single client.dns.lookup mode that expands a DNS alias into its member broker names so SASL authenticates against the real security principal

candidates.title: use_all_dns_ips
candidates.concept_granularity: single client.dns.lookup mode that tries every IP a hostname resolves to, so one unreachable address does not fail the connection

candidates.title: request.timeout.ms
candidates.concept_granularity: single ceiling on how long an application waits for an AdminClient response including retries, defaulting to 120 seconds and worth lowering on a critical path

candidates.title: AdminClient 토픽 관리
candidates.concept_granularity: single family of AdminClient topic operations - list, describe, create and delete - that is the API's most common use

candidates.title: listTopics()
candidates.concept_granularity: single operation returning a ListTopicsResult whose names() Future yields the cluster's topic name set

candidates.title: createTopics()
candidates.concept_granularity: single operation creating topics by name, with partition and replica counts optional and falling back to the broker defaults, whose result must be re-read to confirm the outcome

candidates.title: deleteTopics()
candidates.concept_granularity: single irreversible deletion operation that takes a topic list and performs no emptiness or confirmation check

candidates.title: Future.get() 블로킹
candidates.concept_granularity: single blocking call pattern that is acceptable for the rare admin operation but must be avoided on a server thread expected to serve many admin requests

candidates.title: whenComplete()
candidates.concept_granularity: single non-blocking completion callback that replaces get() so the calling thread serves other requests while Kafka responds

candidates.title: ConfigResource
candidates.concept_granularity: single addressing object naming which broker, broker log or topic a configuration operation targets

candidates.title: describeConfigs()
candidates.concept_granularity: single read operation returning each ConfigResource's settings, where isDefault() is false both for user-set topic values and for values inherited from a modified broker setting

candidates.title: incrementalAlterConfigs()
candidates.concept_granularity: single write operation expressing each change as a config-entry and operation-type pair, so a setting can be set, reset to default, appended to or subtracted from without resending the whole list

uncited_substantive_prose.detail: A note pointing at an outside blog post about Java Future. It asserts nothing about Kafka.
A general definition of 'namespace' using Java packages and Docker as examples. It defines a programming term, not a Kafka concept, so it belongs to no kafka.* concept.

A motivating example plus a callout re-explaining log compaction. kafka.retention.log-compaction is already applied and this span would restate it, so no candidate cites it. kafka.adminclient.topic-existence-check and kafka.adminclient.incremental-alter-configs relate to that concept instead.
Long Java listings whose meaning is carried by the numbered commentary spans that are cited. Citing the listing as well would duplicate the same bytes across two documents.
